[...] The typical presentation of takotsubo cardiomyopathy is chest pain with or without shortness of breath and associated electrocardiogram (ECG) changes mimicking an anterior wall myocardial infarction. [...] It classically mimics ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction [...] The pathophysiology is not well understood, but a sudden massive surge of catecholamines such as adrenaline and noradrenaline from extreme stress or a tumor secreting these chemicals is thought to play a ce [...] The syndrome was first named "takotsubo" by Japanese physician Hikaru Sato, who described "tako-tsubo-like left ventricular dysfunction" in a 1990 case study. The name comes from the Japanese word takotsubo (蛸壷, "octopus trap"), because when affected by this condition, the left ventricle of the heart takes on a shape resembling the round jar used for catching lobsters and octopuses.

gancho: Um pesquisador e três alunos observaram 1.200 pessoas rindo no dia a dia: só 10% a 20% das risadas vieram depois de algo parecido com piada. E quem falava ria quase 50% mais do que quem ouvia.
explicacao: O pesquisador era Robert Provine, estudioso do riso. Com três estudantes de graduação, ele anotava, a cada risada ouvida em lugares como o centro estudantil e as calçadas da cidade, quem estava falando, quem riu e o que tinha sido dito logo antes. O esperado era o riso da plateia depois da tirada de alguém. O que apareceu foi outra coisa: frases banais, como "Onde você estava?" ou "Foi bom te conhecer também", puxavam muito mais risadas do que piadas, e quem falava ria mais do que quem escutava. Para Provine, isso indica que o estímulo decisivo para o riso é outra pessoa, e não o humor. Diários de estudantes reforçaram a ideia: descontado o efeito de TV, rádio e livros, o riso foi 30 vezes mais frequente em companhia do que a sós. Sozinhos, os alunos tendiam mais a falar consigo mesmos ou a sorrir do que a rir. O riso, nessa visão, é um sinal enviado aos outros, e quase some sem plateia. Ele também é difícil de controlar: peça a alguém para rir de propósito e a resposta costuma ser que não dá para rir sob encomenda. Chimpanzés, gorilas e orangotangos também soltam vocalizações parecidas com riso em brincadeiras de luta, perseguição e cócegas.

fontes.titulo: The Science of Laughter (Robert R. Provine, Psychology Today, 2000)
fontes.trecho: As a starting point, three undergraduate students and I observed 1,200 people laughing spontaneously in their natural environments, from the student union to city sidewalks. Whenever we heard laughter, we noted the gender of the speaker (the person talking immediately before laughter occurred) and the audience (those listening to the speaker), whether the speaker or the audience laughed, and what the speaker said immediately before the laughter. While we usually think of laughter as coming from an audience after a wisecrack from a single speaker, contrary to expectation, the speakers we observed laughed almost 50% more than their audiences. The study also showed that banal comments like, "Where have you been?" or "It was nice meeting you, too" -- hardly knee-slappers -- are far more likely to precede laughter than jokes. Only 10% to 20% of the laughter episodes we witnessed followed anything joke-like. [...] This suggests that the critical stimulus for laughter is another person, not a joke. [...] After excluding the vicarious social effects of media (television, radio, books, etc.), its social nature was striking: Laughter was 30 times more frequent in social than solitary situations. The students were much more likely to talk to themselves or even smile when alone than to laugh. However happy we may feel, laughter is a signal we send to others and it virtually disappears when we lack an audience. Laughter is also extremely difficult to control consciously. Try asking a friend to laugh, for example. Most will announce, "I can't laugh on command,"

Laughter researcher Robert Provine said [...] Other than humans, some other species of primate (chimpanzees, gorillas and orangutans) express laughter-like vocalizations in response to physical contact such as wrestling, play chasing or tickling.

gancho: Um estudo de 1978, com 22 ganhadores, virou prova de que a loteria não traz felicidade duradoura. Com 3.362 jogadores suecos, outro estudo achou o contrário: a satisfação com a vida subiu e durou mais de uma década.
explicacao: O estudo antigo, de Philip Brickman e colegas, entrevistou 22 ganhadores de loteria e 29 pessoas que tinham ficado paraplégicas, entre um mês e um ano e meio depois do evento. Os ganhadores disseram estar mais ou menos tão felizes quanto antes. O trabalho virou exemplo da "esteira hedônica", a ideia de que, passado o impacto inicial de algo muito bom ou muito ruim, as pessoas voltam ao seu nível habitual de felicidade. Em 2018, os economistas Erik Lindqvist, Robert Östling e David Cesarini publicaram um teste bem maior. Eles ouviram 3.362 jogadores de loterias suecas, de 5 a 22 anos depois do prêmio, com US$ 277 milhões distribuídos no total. Como o valor ganho é sorteado dentro de cada grupo de jogadores, comparar quem levou mais com quem levou menos funciona como um experimento, e as análises seguiram um plano registrado de antemão. Os grandes ganhadores mostraram um aumento sustentado na satisfação com a vida, sem sinal de que ele diminuísse com o tempo. O efeito sobre a felicidade do dia a dia e a saúde mental foi bem menor, e a satisfação com as finanças parece ser o elo principal. Outros estudos grandes também mostram que divórcio, viuvez e desemprego mudam o bem-estar a longo prazo, apesar de alguma adaptação.

fontes.trecho: Brickman, Coates, and Janoff-Bulman were among the first to investigate the hedonic treadmill in their 1978 study, "Lottery Winners and Accident Victims: Is Happiness Relative?". Lottery winners and paraplegics were compared to a control group and as predicted, comparison (with past experiences and current communities) and habituation (to new circumstances) affected levels of happiness such that after the initial impact of the extremely positive or negative events, happiness levels typically went back to the average levels. [...] In large panel studies, divorce, death of a spouse, unemployment, disability, and similar events have been shown to change long-term subjective well-being, even though some adaptation does occur. In the aforementioned Brickman study (1978), researchers interviewed 22 lottery winners and 29 paraplegics to determine their change in happiness levels due to their given event (winning the lottery or becoming paralyzed). The event in the case of lottery winners had taken place between one month and one and a half years before the study, and in the case of paraplegics between a month and a year. The lottery winners reported being similarly happy before and after the event

fontes.titulo: Long-run Effects of Lottery Wealth on Psychological Well-being (Lindqvist, Östling e Cesarini, NBER Working Paper 24667, 2018)
fontes.trecho: May 2018 [...] We surveyed a large sample of Swedish lottery players about their psychological well-being and analyzed the data following pre-registered procedures. Relative to matched controls, large-prize winners experience sustained increases in overall life satisfaction that persist for over a decade and show no evidence of dissipating with time. The estimated treatment effects on happiness and mental health are significantly smaller [...] financial life satisfaction as an important mediator for the long-run increase in overall life satisfaction. [...] We surveyed lottery players about their well-being 5 to 22 years after the lottery event. [...] our data allow us classify players into groups within which we know the prize amount won is randomly assigned. Our estimates are based entirely on comparisons of players who are in the same group but were awarded prizes of diﬀerent magnitudes. Second, because of the large sample size (3,362 players) and substantial prize pool ($277 million)

gancho: Num experimento de 1983, um sinal cerebral ligado a um gesto simples surgiu centenas de milissegundos antes de a pessoa sentir que decidia fazê-lo. O que isso diz sobre o livre-arbítrio ainda é disputa aberta.
explicacao: Benjamin Libet, pesquisador da Universidade da Califórnia em São Francisco, pedia a voluntários que apertassem um botão ou flexionassem o pulso quando quisessem, enquanto eletrodos no couro cabeludo registravam a atividade do córtex. Para marcar o instante da decisão, eles olhavam um ponto que girava num osciloscópio, como o ponteiro de um relógio, e diziam onde ele estava quando sentiram a vontade de agir. Em média, essa vontade consciente surgia uns 200 milissegundos antes do movimento. Já um sinal elétrico de preparação, o potencial de prontidão, aparecia cerca de meio segundo antes. Para alguns, isso mostra que processos inconscientes iniciam a ação e a consciência só fica sabendo depois. O próprio Libet discordava: para ele, ainda sobrava tempo para vetar o gesto. A leitura do experimento também foi contestada. Num estudo publicado em 2012, Aaron Schurger e colegas propuseram que o potencial de prontidão pode nascer de flutuações espontâneas da atividade neural, e não de uma decisão inconsciente. Em 2019, outro estudo não o encontrou em decisões deliberadas, só nas arbitrárias. Não há acordo sobre o que o experimento significa.

fontes.trecho: Libet was a researcher in the physiology department of the University of California, San Francisco. [...] instruct the subject to carry out some small, simple motor activity, such as pressing a button, or flexing a finger or wrist [...] the output was a single dot that could be made to travel in a circular motion, similar to the movements of a second hand around a clock face. [...] the subject would be asked to note the position of the dot on the oscilloscope timer when "he/she was first aware of the wish or urge to act" [...] On average, approximately two hundred milliseconds elapsed between the first appearance of conscious will to press the button and the act of pressing it. [...] occurred, on average, approximately five hundred milliseconds before the trial ended with the pushing of the button. That is to say, researchers recorded mounting brain activity related to the resultant action as many as three hundred milliseconds before subjects reported the first awareness of conscious will to act. [...] There is no majority agreement about the interpretation or the significance of Libet's experiments. However, Libet's experiments suggest to some that unconscious processes in the brain are the true initiator of volitional acts [...] Libet himself regards his experimental results to be entirely compatible with the notion of free will. He finds that conscious volition is exercised in the form of 'the power of veto' [...] Since the subjective experience of the conscious will to act preceded the action by only 200 milliseconds [...] In a study published in 2012, Aaron Schurger, Jacobo D. Sitt, and Stanislas Dehaene proposed that the occurrence of the readiness potentials observed in Libet-type experiments is stochastically occasioned by ongoing spontaneous subthreshold fluctuations in neural activity, rather than an unconscious goal-directed operation. In an empirical study in 2019, researchers found that readiness potentials were absent for deliberate decisions, and preceded arbitrary decisions only.
One of the pioneering studies in this field was conducted by Benjamin Libet and his colleagues in 1983

gancho: Um paciente com os hemisférios do cérebro desconectados viu, em cada metade da visão, um pé de galinha e uma paisagem com neve. Escolheu uma pá para a neve, mas explicou: "a pá é para limpar o galinheiro".
explicacao: A cirurgia que produz o "cérebro dividido" corta o corpo caloso, o feixe de fibras que liga os dois hemisférios, e é um último recurso contra epilepsias graves. Num relato de 1967, Roger Sperry e Michael Gazzaniga descreveram como as duas metades passavam a funcionar de forma independente; Sperry ganhou o Nobel de Medicina de 1981. No teste clássico, cada imagem chega a só um hemisfério. O paciente associa corretamente a galinha ao pé e a pá à neve, mas, perguntado sobre a pá, responde falando da galinha. Gazzaniga chamou de "intérprete" esse sistema do hemisfério esquerdo que monta uma explicação plausível para a ação sem saber o que o outro lado recebeu, e depois se viu que ele age também em pessoas comuns. A visão consagrada dizia que cortar o corpo caloso dá a cada hemisfério uma consciência própria. Em 2017, um estudo da Universidade de Amsterdã com dois pacientes contestou isso: eles conseguiam dizer se havia um objeto e onde ele estava, em qualquer parte do campo visual, respondendo com qualquer uma das mãos ou falando. Para os autores, a percepção se divide, mas continua havendo um só agente consciente. A questão segue em debate.

fontes.trecho: The surgical operation to produce this condition (corpus callosotomy) involves transection of the corpus callosum, and is usually a last resort to treat refractory epilepsy. [...] This makes first-person accounts hard to consider and to assess as scientists do not know if the consciousness was split as well. [...] For example, a patient with split brain is shown a picture of a chicken foot and a snowy field in separate visual fields and asked to choose from a list of words the best association with the pictures. The patient would choose a chicken to associate with the chicken foot and a shovel to associate with the snow; however, when asked to reason why the patient chose the shovel, the response would relate to the chicken (e.g. "the shovel is for cleaning out the chicken coop"). [...] Sperry earned the 1981 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his contributions in hemispheric specialization. Sperry initiated split-brain research and his colleague, Michael Gazzaniga, helped him summarize their findings. Their report in the 1967 Scientific American report titled, "The Split Brain in Man," examined how the two hemispheres function independently of one another after a corpus callosotomy.

It refers to the construction of explanations by the left brain hemisphere in order to make sense of the world by reconciling new information with what was known before. [...] Although the concept of the left-brain interpreter was initially based on experiments on patients with split-brains, it has since been shown to apply to the everyday behavior of people at large. [...] The left-brain interpreter will nonetheless construct a contrived explanation for the action, unaware of the instruction the right brain had received.

fontes.titulo: Split brain does not lead to split consciousness (ScienceDaily, 2017, release da Universiteit van Amsterdam)
fontes.trecho: January 25, 2017 [...] A new research study contradicts the established view that so-called split-brain patients have a split consciousness. [...] This was taken as evidence that severing the corpus callosum causes each hemisphere to gain its own consciousness. For their study, Pinto and his fellow researchers conducted a series of tests on two patients who had undergone a full callosotomy. [...] To the researchers’ surprise, the patients were able to respond to stimuli throughout the entire visual field with all the response types: left hand, right hand and verbally. [...] Our findings, however, reveal that although the two hemispheres are completely insulated from each other, the brain as a whole is still able to produce only one conscious agent.

gancho: Em 1998, o neurocientista Christof Koch apostou com o filósofo David Chalmers que em 25 anos se saberia como os neurônios produzem a consciência. Em 2023, Koch admitiu a derrota e pagou com uma caixa de vinho.
explicacao: Chalmers ficou famoso por batizar, numa palestra de 1994 em Tucson, o "problema difícil" da consciência: explicar por que e como os organismos têm experiência subjetiva, e não só a capacidade de perceber e agir. Koch, que trabalhou durante anos com Francis Crick na busca pelos correlatos neurais da consciência, apostou que o mecanismo seria descoberto até 2023. Chalmers apostou no contrário. Em 23 de junho de 2023, no encontro anual da Associação para o Estudo Científico da Consciência, em Nova York, os dois concordaram em público que a busca continua, e Chalmers foi declarado vencedor. No mesmo mês saíram os primeiros resultados de um confronto combinado entre rivais: desde 2019, uma fundação investia mais de 6 milhões de dólares para confrontar previsões opostas de duas teorias rivais, a da informação integrada (IIT) e a do espaço de trabalho neuronal global (GNWT). Os criadores das duas aprovaram de antemão os protocolos e as condições de acerto. Nenhuma previsão da GNWT passou no critério combinado; da IIT, duas de três passaram. Os resultados finais saíram na Nature em 2025, e a disputa entre as teorias segue aberta.

fontes.titulo: Decades-long bet on consciousness ends — and it's philosopher 1, neuroscientist 0 (Nature, 2023)
fontes.trecho: In 1998, neuroscientist Christof Koch bet philosopher David Chalmers that the mechanism by which the brain’s neurons produce consciousness would be discovered by 2023. Both scientists agreed publicly on 23 June, at the annual meeting of the Association for the Scientific Study of Consciousness (ASSC) in New York City, that it is an ongoing quest — and declared Chalmers the winner.

Koch's primary collaborator in the endeavor of locating the neural correlates of consciousness was the molecular biologist turned neuroscientist, Francis Crick [...] In 2023, Koch lost a 25-year bet to philosopher David Chalmers. Koch bet that the neural underpinnings of consciousness will be well-understood by 2023, while Chalmers bet the contrary. Upon losing, Koch gifted Chalmers a case of fine wine.

the hard problem of consciousness (or simply the hard problem) is to explain how and why organisms have qualia, phenomenal consciousness, or subjective experience. [...] The terms "hard problem" and "easy problems" were coined by the philosopher David Chalmers in a 1994 talk given at The Science of Consciousness conference held in Tucson, Arizona.

In 2019, the Templeton Foundation announced funding in excess of $6,000,000 to test opposing empirical predictions of IIT and a rival theory (Global Neuronal Workspace Theory, GNWT). The originators of both theories signed off on experimental protocols and data analyses as well as the exact conditions that satisfy if their championed theory correctly predicted the outcome or not. Initial results were revealed in June 2023. None of GNWT's predictions passed what was agreed upon pre-registration while two out of three of IIT's predictions passed that threshold. The final, peer-reviewed results were published in the 30 April 2025 issue of Nature.

gancho: Pela teoria da informação integrada, uma das mais debatidas sobre a consciência, portas lógicas inativas arranjadas do jeito certo seriam conscientes, até mais que um ser humano. O criador da teoria aceita a conclusão.
explicacao: A teoria da informação integrada, a IIT, foi proposta pelo neurocientista Giulio Tononi em 2004. Ela tenta explicar a experiência consciente de um sistema físico a partir de todo o seu poder de causa e efeito, e mede isso com uma grandeza chamada Φ (fi). O cientista da computação Scott Aaronson usou a própria formulação da teoria como crítica: mostrou que uma série de portas lógicas inativas, bem arranjada, seria não só consciente, mas "ilimitadamente mais consciente que os humanos". Tononi concordou com a conta e foi além: um arranjo ainda mais simples, se fosse grande o bastante, também seria consciente. Para ele, isso é um ponto forte, porque grandes partes do córtex, sobretudo na parte de trás do cérebro, têm justamente esse tipo de organização. Muitos não se convenceram. Em setembro de 2023, uma carta assinada por 124 pesquisadores defendeu que a IIT fosse chamada de pseudociência enquanto não pudesse ser testada. Outros saíram em defesa da teoria, e numa enquete anônima com 60 pesquisadores da área só 8% concordaram totalmente com a carta.

fontes.trecho: it should be possible to account for the conscious experience of a physical system by unfolding its complete causal powers. IIT was proposed by neuroscientist Giulio Tononi in 2004. [...] computational barriers to calculating Φ, the measure of high complexity used in IIT. [...] A letter published on 15 September 2023 in the preprint repository PsyArXiv and signed by 124 scholars asserted that until IIT is empirically testable, it should be labeled pseudoscience. A number of researchers defended the theory in response. [...] Of the 60 respondents, 8% "fully" agreed, and 20% did "not at all" agree with the letter [...] Theoretical computer scientist Scott Aaronson has criticized IIT by demonstrating through its own formulation that an inactive series of logic gates, arranged in the correct way, would not only be conscious but be "unboundedly more conscious than humans are." Tononi himself agrees with the assessment and argues that according to IIT, an even simpler arrangement of inactive logic gates, if large enough, would also be conscious. However he further argues that this is a strength of IIT rather than a weakness, because that's exactly the sort of cytoarchitecture followed by large portions of the cerebral cortex, specially at the back of the brain

gancho: Em 2006, uma paciente que não reagia a nada, tida como em estado vegetativo, recebeu num aparelho de ressonância o pedido de imaginar que jogava tênis. A atividade do cérebro dela mudou sob comando.
explicacao: O estudo, do neurocientista britânico Adrian Owen, saiu na revista Science e mostrou que alguns pacientes considerados vegetativos estão, na verdade, conscientes. O fenômeno ganhou o nome de consciência encoberta, ou dissociação cognitivo-motora: a pessoa entende e obedece, mas o corpo não consegue mostrar. Em 2010, a equipe usou um método parecido para que um homem tido como vegetativo havia mais de 5 anos respondesse "sim" e "não" a perguntas apenas mudando a atividade cerebral. Faltava saber se esses casos eram raros. Em 2024, um estudo internacional publicado no New England Journal of Medicine avaliou 353 adultos com distúrbios de consciência. Por ressonância funcional ou eletroencefalograma, eles recebiam pedidos como "continue mexendo os dedos dos pés" ou "balance o braço como se jogasse tênis". Entre os 241 que não davam nenhuma resposta visível aos comandos, um em cada quatro (25%) produziu os mesmos padrões de atividade cerebral que pessoas saudáveis. A descoberta pesa no diagnóstico, nos cuidados e até nas decisões sobre manter ou não a vida após lesões graves.

fontes.trecho: Adrian Mark Owen (born 17 May 1966) is a British and Canadian neuroscientist and best-selling author. He is best known for his 2006 discovery, published in the journal Science showing that some patients thought to be in a vegetative state are in fact fully aware [...] Owen is credited with discovering 'covert awareness' (sometimes referred to as 'cognitive motor dissociation') by showing for the first time that a behaviourally non-responsive (vegetative state) patient could change her pattern of brain activity 'on command' when was asked to imagine playing a game of tennis in an fMRI scanner. This landmark discovery has had implications for clinical care, diagnosis, medical ethics and medical/legal decision-making (relating to the prolongation, or otherwise, of life after severe brain injury). In a follow-up paper in 2010 in The New England Journal of Medicine, Owen and his team used a similar method to allow a man believed to be in a vegetative state for more than 5 years to answer 'yes' and 'no' questions with responses that were generated solely by changing his brain activity using fMRI.

fontes.titulo: One in four patients in vegetative or minimally conscious state able to perform cognitive tasks, study finds (University of Cambridge, 2024)
fontes.trecho: researchers across Europe and North America recruited a total of 353 adults with disorders of consciousness [...] Researchers assessed patterns of brain activation among these patients using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) or electroencephalography (EEG). Subjects were asked to repeatedly imagine performing a motor activity (for example, “keep wiggling your toes”, “swinging your arm as if playing tennis”, [...] The results of the study are published today in the New England Journal of Medicine. [...] Among the 241 patients with a prolonged disorder of consciousness, who could not make any visible responses to bedside commands, one in four (25%) was able to perform cognitive tasks, producing the same patterns of brain activity recorded with EEG and/or fMRI that are seen in healthy subjects in response to the same instructions.

fontes.titulo: Study Detects Cognitive Motor Dissociation in Patients With Disorders of Consciousness (HealthDay, 2024)
fontes.trecho: FRIDAY, Aug. 16, 2024 (HealthDay News) -- Cognitive motor dissociation is seen in about 25 percent of individuals with disorders of consciousness without an observable response to commands, according to a study published in the Aug. 15 issue of the New England Journal of Medicine.

gancho: Depois de um AVC em 1995, o editor da revista Elle Jean-Dominique Bauby só conseguia mexer a pálpebra esquerda. Piscando a cada letra, ditou um livro inteiro. Morreu dois dias depois de ele ser publicado.
explicacao: Bauby teve o derrame em 8 de dezembro de 1995, aos 43 anos, enquanto dirigia levando o filho ao teatro. Acordou no hospital 20 dias depois com a síndrome do encarceramento: as faculdades mentais ficam intactas, mas quase todo o corpo fica paralisado. No caso dele, a boca, os braços e as pernas. Antes do AVC, ele tinha assinado contrato para escrever um livro. A fonoaudióloga Sandrine Fichou organizou as 26 letras do alfabeto pela frequência de uso, para agilizar o ditado. Claude Mendibil, enviada pela editora, recitava essa sequência, e Bauby piscava quando ela chegava à letra certa. Assim, uma letra de cada vez, ela registrou as 130 páginas do manuscrito, trabalhando três horas por dia, sete dias por semana, durante dois meses. "O escafandro e a borboleta" saiu numa sexta-feira, 7 de março de 1997, chegou ao primeiro lugar das listas de mais vendidos na Europa e já vendeu milhões de exemplares. Bauby morreu de pneumonia dois dias depois do lançamento, aos 44 anos. Em 2007, o livro virou filme, dirigido por Julian Schnabel.

fontes.trecho: On 8 December 1995, at the age of 43, Bauby had a stroke while driving his son to a night out at the theatre. When he woke up in the hospital 20 days later, he could only blink his left eyelid. He had locked-in syndrome, in which the mental faculties remain intact but most of the body is paralyzed. In Bauby's case, his mouth, arms, and legs were paralyzed [...] Before his stroke, Bauby had signed a contract to write a book. His speech therapist, Sandrine Fichou, arranged a 26-letter alphabet according to the frequency of use so he could dictate. Claude Mendibil, a ghostwriter and freelance book editor, was sent by his publisher Robert Laffont to take the dictation using a system called partner-assisted scanning. She recited the alphabet until Bauby blinked at the correct letter, and recorded the 130-page manuscript letter by letter over the course of two months, working three hours a day, seven days a week. The resulting book, The Diving Bell and the Butterfly, was published on Friday, 7 March 1997. It went on to become a number one bestseller across Europe and its total sales are now in the millions. At the age of 44, Bauby died from pneumonia, two days after the publishing of his book. [...] In 2007, painter and director Julian Schnabel released a film version of The Diving Bell and the Butterfly

gancho: A anestesia geral é usada em cirurgias desde o século XIX, e ainda não se sabe bem como ela apaga a consciência. E ela age até em plantas: anestesiada, a dioneia não fecha a armadilha quando é tocada.
explicacao: Em 1842, o médico Crawford Long deu éter a um paciente e fez uma operação sem dor. Desde então, muitas substâncias sem nenhuma semelhança química entre si se mostraram anestésicas. Até o xenônio funciona: é um gás nobre, que em geral não reage com quase nada, e foi usado numa cirurgia pela primeira vez em 1951. Em 1899, Hans Horst Meyer notou, testando girinos, que quanto mais um anestésico se dissolve em azeite de oliva, mais potente ele é; Charles Overton chegou à mesma ideia de forma independente. Hoje se sabe que vários anestésicos agem sobre proteínas dos neurônios, como o receptor GABA-A, mas eles têm muitos alvos possíveis, e o mecanismo bioquímico da anestesia geral ainda não é totalmente compreendido. Um estudo de 2017, na revista Annals of Botany, acrescentou um enigma: expostas a anestésicos, várias plantas perderam os movimentos espontâneos e os provocados pelo toque. A dioneia deixou de gerar sinais elétricos, e as gavinhas da ervilha ficaram paradas, enroladas. Para os autores, a ação dos anestésicos em células e órgãos é parecida em plantas e animais, e plantas poderiam servir para testar anestésicos.

fontes.trecho: The biochemical mechanism of action of general anaesthetics is not fully understood. Anaesthetics have myriad sites of action and affect the central nervous system (CNS) at several levels.

General anaesthetics have been widely used in surgery since 1842 when Crawford Long for the first time administered diethyl ether to a patient and performed a painless operation. [...] In general, different anaesthetics exhibit different mechanisms of action such that there are numerous non-exclusionary molecular targets at all levels of integration within the central nervous system. However, for certain intravenous anaesthetics, such as propofol and etomidate, the main molecular target is believed to be GABAA receptor [...] In 1899 Hans Horst Meyer published the first experimental evidence of the fact that anaesthetic potency is related to lipid solubility. Two years later a similar theory was published independently by Charles Ernest Overton. Meyer compared the potency of many agents, defined as the reciprocal of the molar concentration required to induce anaesthesia in tadpoles, with their olive oil/water partition coefficient. [...] the greater the lipid solubility of a compound in olive oil, the greater its anaesthetic potency.

odorless noble gas found in Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts. Although generally unreactive, it can undergo a few chemical reactions [...] Xenon was first used as a surgical anesthetic in 1951 by American anesthesiologist Stuart C. Cullen

fontes.titulo: Anesthetics have the same effects on plants as they have on animals and humans (Oxford University Press, EurekAlert, 2017)
fontes.trecho: 11-Dec-2017 [...] A new study published in Annals of Botany shows that plants react to anesthetics similarly to the way animals and humans do [...] Since then many different chemicals have been found to induce anesthesia. However, despite the fact that many anesthetics have been used over a 150-year period, little is known about how these different compounds with no structural similarities behave as anesthetic agents inducing loss of consciousness. Remarkably, as found in the new study, anesthetics also work on plants. Researchers found that, when exposed to anesthetics, a number of plants lost both their autonomous and touch-induced movements. Venus flytraps no longer generate electrical signals and their traps remain open when trigger hairs were touched, and growing pea tendrils stopped their autonomous movements and were immobilized in a curled shape. The results of this study suggest that the action of anesthetic at cellular and organ levels are similar in plants and animals. This study suggests that plants are emerging as model objects to study general questions related to anesthetics, as well as to serve as a suitable alternative test system for human anesthesia.

gancho: Depois de certos AVCs, a pessoa fica com metade do corpo paralisada e não percebe. Um jato de água gelada no ouvido esquerdo pode, por algum tempo, diminuir essa cegueira para a própria deficiência.
explicacao: O nome do fenômeno é anosognosia, do grego "sem conhecimento da doença". O termo foi criado em 1914 pelo neurologista Joseph Babinski para descrever quem não se dava conta da própria hemiplegia, a paralisia de um lado do corpo. Parece negação psicológica, mas resulta de lesões físicas, em geral no lobo parietal ou em áreas do hemisfério direito, e não parece decorrer diretamente da perda de sensação: o dano estaria nos processos que juntam as informações dos sentidos com a representação do próprio corpo. Pode ser seletiva: alguém com várias deficiências às vezes ignora só uma e reconhece as outras. Na fase aguda do AVC, a falta de noção de uma fraqueza num lado do corpo é estimada entre 10% e 18% dos casos. A água gelada no ouvido estimula intensamente o sistema vestibular, o do equilíbrio, e melhora por um tempo tanto a anosognosia quanto a negligência espacial, em que a pessoa ignora um lado do espaço. Não está claro por quê: uma hipótese é que a estimulação desloca a atenção sem que a pessoa perceba. Não existe tratamento de longo prazo, e muitos casos simplesmente desaparecem com o tempo.

fontes.trecho: Anosognosia results from physiological damage to brain structures, typically to the parietal lobe or a diffuse lesion on the fronto-temporal-parietal area in the right hemisphere [...] the term was coined by the neurologist Joseph Babinski in 1914, in order to describe the unawareness of hemiplegia. Phenomenologically, anosognosia has similarities to denial, which is a psychological defense mechanism [...] The name derives from Ancient Greek [...] anosognosia for hemiparesis (weakness of one side of the body) with onset of acute stroke is estimated at between 10% and 18%. [...] The condition does not seem to be directly related to sensory loss but is thought to be caused by damage to higher level neurocognitive processes that are involved in integrating sensory information with processes that support spatial or bodily representations [...] people seem unable to attend to, or sometimes comprehend, anything on a certain side of their body (usually the left). Anosognosia can be selective in that an affected person with multiple impairments may seem unaware of only one handicap, while appearing to be fully aware of any others. [...] In regard to anosognosia for neurological patients, no long-term treatments exist. As with unilateral neglect, caloric reflex testing (squirting ice cold water into the left ear) is known to temporarily ameliorate unawareness of impairment. It is not entirely clear how this works, although it is thought that the unconscious shift of attention or focus caused by the intense stimulation of the vestibular system temporarily influences awareness. Most cases of anosognosia appear to simply disappear over time

gancho: Depois de um acidente de moto, um escocês se convenceu de que tinha morrido. Levado pela mãe à África do Sul, achou que estava no inferno, e o calor só confirmava. É a síndrome de Cotard.
explicacao: O neurologista e psiquiatra Jules Cotard descreveu em 1880 o que chamou de "delírio das negações". Sua paciente, a "Mademoiselle X", negava a existência de partes do próprio corpo e a necessidade de comer. Dizia estar condenada à danação eterna e, por isso, não poder morrer de morte natural. Acabou morrendo de fome. O caso do escocês, que tinha sofrido lesão cerebral no acidente, foi descrito num artigo de 1996. Depois de sair do hospital em Edimburgo, em janeiro de 1990, ele achava que tinha morrido de uma infecção generalizada, ou talvez de aids, e que tinha "pegado emprestado" o espírito da mãe para conhecer o inferno, enquanto ela dormia na Escócia. Uma hipótese liga a síndrome à de Capgras, em que parentes parecem impostores: nas duas, um rosto é reconhecido, mas sem a sensação de familiaridade que costuma vir junto. Diante do próprio rosto, a pessoa deixaria de senti-lo como seu e concluiria que não existe. A síndrome aparece sobretudo em psicoses, como a esquizofrenia, e também na depressão.

fontes.trecho: In 1880, the neurologist and psychiatrist Jules Cotard described the condition as le délire des négations ("the delusion of negation") [...] The case of "Mademoiselle X" describes a woman who denied the existence of parts of her body (somatoparaphrenia) and of her need to eat. She claimed that she was condemned to eternal damnation and therefore could not die a natural death. In the course of experiencing "the delusion of negation", Mademoiselle X died of starvation. [...] The article Betwixt Life and Death: Case Studies of the Cotard Delusion (1996) describes a contemporary case of Cotard's syndrome which occurred in a Scotsman whose brain was damaged in a motorcycle accident: [...] In January 1990, after his discharge from hospital in Edinburgh, his mother took him to South Africa. He was convinced that he had been taken to Hell (which was confirmed by the heat) and that he had died of sepsis (which had been a risk early in his recovery), or perhaps from AIDS [...] He thought he had "borrowed [his] mother's spirit to show [him] around Hell" and that she was asleep in Scotland. [...] Neurologically, Cotard's syndrome (negation of the self) is thought to be related to Capgras delusion (people replaced by impostors) [...] ks the familiarity (recognition) normally associated with it. [...] If the patient sees their own face, they might perceive no association between the face and their own sense of self⁠—which results in the patient believing that they do not exist (Cotard's syndrome). Cotard's syndrome is usually encountered in people with psychosis, as in schizophrenia. It is also found in clinical depression

gancho: Imagine uma maçã vermelha. Algumas pessoas não veem nada: não conseguem formar imagens na mente, e muita gente se espanta ao descobrir que isso não é universal. A condição só ganhou nome, afantasia, em 2015.
explicacao: A condição ganhou nome em 2015: afantasia, do grego "sem imagem", termo criado pela equipe do neurologista Adam Zeman, da Universidade de Exeter. A pesquisa moderna começou em 2005, quando um homem o procurou dizendo ter perdido a capacidade de visualizar depois de uma pequena cirurgia. O caso foi publicado em 2010, e logo várias pessoas escreveram a Zeman contando que nunca tinham conseguido. O fenômeno já tinha sido descrito em 1880 por Francis Galton, num estudo estatístico sobre imagens mentais. Um teste simples é imaginar uma maçã vermelha e dar nota de 1 (nítida como foto) a 5 (nada). Quando ele se espalhou pelas redes sociais em 2020, muita gente se chocou ao saber que a própria capacidade, ou incapacidade, de visualizar não é universal. Um estudo de 2022 estimou que 0,8% da população não forma imagens visuais. Curiosamente, a maioria dos participantes do estudo de 2015 relatava imagens involuntárias, como as dos sonhos.

fontes.trecho: is the inability to voluntarily visualize mental images. [...] Interest in the phenomenon was renewed after the publication of a study in 2015 by a team led by the neurologist Adam Zeman of the University of Exeter. Zeman's team coined the term aphantasia, derived from the Ancient Greek word phantasia [...] The phenomenon was first described by Francis Galton in 1880, in a statistical study on mental imagery. Galton wrote: To my astonishment, I found that the great majority of the men of science to whom I first applied, protested that mental imagery was unknown to them, and they looked on me as fanciful and fantastic [...] They had no more notion of its true nature than a colour-blind man who has not discerned his defect has of the nature of colour. [...] The phenomenon remained largely unstudied until 2005, when Professor Adam Zeman of the University of Exeter was approached by a man who seemed to have lost the ability to visualize after undergoing minor surgery. Following the publication of this patient's case in 2010, a number of people approached Zeman reporting a lifelong inability to visualize. [...] One way of considering aphantasia is to ask a person to imagine a red apple (or red star) and rate their "mind's eye" depiction of it on a scale from 1 (photographic visualisation) through to 5 (no visualisation at all). Such a test was popularised on social media in 2020. Many people are shocked to learn that their own ability or inability to visualise objects is not universal. [...] He found that most aphantasics lack voluntary visualizations only; the majority of test subjects did report involuntary visualizations such as dreams. [...] A 2022 study estimated the prevalence of aphantasia among the general population [...] They found that 0.8% of the population was unable to form visual mental images

gancho: Em 2021, equipes de quatro países conversaram com pessoas adormecidas: em pleno sonho lúcido, elas ouviam perguntas como "quanto é 8 menos 6?" e respondiam com movimentos dos olhos.
explicacao: No sonho lúcido, a pessoa sabe que está sonhando. O termo foi criado em 1913 pelo psiquiatra holandês Frederik van Eeden. Uma das primeiras provas de laboratório veio de um truque com os olhos, que continuam se mexendo no sono REM. Por volta das 8 da manhã de 12 de abril de 1975, o pesquisador Keith Hearne registrou uma sequência combinada de movimentos oculares feita de dentro de um sonho lúcido de Alan Worsley. O estudo de 2021, publicado na revista Current Biology, tornou a comunicação de mão dupla. Equipes da França, da Alemanha, da Holanda e dos EUA mandaram perguntas faladas ou contas em código Morse, com luzes e sons, e os sonhadores responderam movendo os olhos ou contraindo músculos do rosto. Houve 29 respostas corretas, de 6 pessoas. Um participante contou depois que as contas pareciam vir de "uma espécie de rádio no carro". O canal ainda é falho: das 158 tentativas feitas durante sonhos lúcidos confirmados, só 18,4% tiveram resposta certa, e na maioria não houve resposta nenhuma. Mesmo assim, abre um jeito novo de estudar os sonhos enquanto acontecem, sem depender só do relato ao acordar.

fontes.titulo: Real-time dialogue between experimenters and dreamers during REM sleep (Konkoly et al., Current Biology, 2021)
fontes.trecho: Here we show that individuals who are asleep and in the midst of a lucid dream (aware of the fact that they are currently dreaming) can perceive questions from an experimenter and provide answers using electrophysiological signals. [...] constituting correctly answered questions on 29 occasions across 6 of the individuals tested. [...] achieved by four independent scientific teams in France, Germany, the Netherlands, and the USA. [...] the source of the math problems “felt like a sort of radio in the car.” [...] We attempted to communicate with the dreamer on a total of 158 occasions during signal-verified lucid dreams. [...] Across all teams, we observed a correct response on 18.4% of these trials [...] The most common outcome was a lack of a response [...] what is 8 minus 6? [...] corresponding to a Morse-coded math problem “4 minus 0.”

fontes.titulo: Real-time dialogue with a dreaming person is possible (ScienceDaily, release da Cell Press, 2021)
fontes.trecho: Real-time dialogue between experimenters and dreamers during REM sleep. Current Biology, 2021

The term lucid dream was coined by Dutch author and psychiatrist Frederik van Eeden in his 1913 article A Study of Dreams [...] In 1975, Dr. Keith Hearne had the idea to exploit the nature of rapid eye movements (REM) to allow a dreamer to send a message directly from dreams to the waking world. Working with an experienced lucid dreamer (Alan Worsley), he eventually succeeded in recording (via the use of an electrooculogram or EOG) a pre-defined set of eye movements signaled from within Worsley's lucid dream. This occurred at around 8 am on the morning of April 12, 1975.

gancho: Em 1982, um filósofo imaginou Mary, cientista que sabe tudo sobre cores, mas só viveu num mundo preto e branco. Ao ver o vermelho, ela aprende algo? Anos depois, o próprio autor abandonou o argumento.
explicacao: O experimento mental é de Frank Jackson, no artigo "Epiphenomenal Qualia", de 1982. Mary tem acesso a todas as descrições físicas das cores, mas nunca teve a experiência de enxergar uma. A pergunta é se, ao sair do mundo sem cor e ver as cores pela primeira vez, ela ganha um conhecimento novo. Se ganha, parece haver algo na experiência que a física não captura. O alvo era o fisicalismo, a visão de que tudo no universo, inclusive a mente, é físico. Para Jackson, a conclusão "irresistível" era que existem mais propriedades do que os fisicalistas reconhecem. No mesmo artigo, ele criou um segundo personagem, Fred, que distingue dois vermelhos diferentes onde a visão comum só vê um. O debate rendeu até um livro, de 2004, com respostas de filósofos como Daniel Dennett, David Lewis e Paul Churchland. A reviravolta veio do próprio autor: Jackson acabou se declarando fisicalista e, numa entrevista de 2023, disse que não aceita mais o argumento. Mesmo assim, acha que quem é fisicalista precisa enfrentá-lo "muito a sério".

fontes.trecho: is a thought experiment proposed by Frank Jackson in his article "Epiphenomenal Qualia" (1982) [...] The thought experiment describes Mary, a scientist who exists in a black-and-white world where she has extensive access to physical descriptions of color, but no actual perceptual experience of color. [...] The central question of the thought experiment is whether Mary will gain new knowledge when she goes outside the colorless world and experiences seeing in color. The thought experiment is intended to argue against physicalism—the view that the universe, including all that is mental, is entirely physical. Jackson says that the "irresistible conclusion" is that "there are more properties than physicalists talk about". Jackson would eventually call himself a physicalist and say, in 2023, "I no longer accept the argument" though he feels that the argument should be "addressed really seriously if you are a physicalist". The debate that emerged following its publication became the subject of an edited volume, There's Something About Mary (2004), which includes replies from such philosophers as Daniel Dennett, David Lewis, and Paul Churchland. [...] The other is a gifted person called "Fred" who "has better colour vision than anyone else on record"; Specifically, Fred can see two different colours of red where ordinary colour vision only sees one.

gancho: Em 1987, um canadense dirigiu uns 20 km de madrugada, matou a sogra e se entregou à polícia. Foi absolvido: especialistas concluíram que estava sonâmbulo, e a Suprema Corte do Canadá manteve a decisão.
explicacao: Na madrugada de 24 de maio de 1987, Kenneth Parks saiu de carro de Pickering até a casa dos sogros em Scarborough, em Ontário. Entrou com uma chave que eles lhe tinham dado, matou a sogra a golpes de chave de roda e tentou, sem sucesso, estrangular o sogro. Coberto de sangue, dirigiu direto a uma delegacia próxima e disse: "Acho que acabei de matar duas pessoas". No julgamento, a defesa alegou automatismo: ele agia dormindo, sem controle voluntário. Um médico depôs que Parks sofria de um distúrbio do sono, e não de doença neurológica ou psiquiátrica, e cinco especialistas em neurologia confirmaram o sonambulismo. O júri o absolveu. A Suprema Corte do Canadá precisou decidir se o sonambulismo devia contar como "doença da mente", o que levaria a um veredito de inimputabilidade por insanidade. Em 1992, os juízes mantiveram a absolvição, porque havia dúvida razoável de que Parks tivesse agido voluntariamente, e concordaram em não tratar o sonambulismo dele como transtorno mental. A decisão virou referência sobre a defesa de automatismo.

fontes.trecho: R v Parks, [1992] 2 S.C.R. 871 is a leading Supreme Court of Canada decision on the criminal automatism defence. In the early morning of May 24, 1987, Kenneth Parks drove 20 kilometres from Pickering, Ontario, to the house of his in-laws in Scarborough, Ontario. He entered their house with a key they had previously given him and used a tire iron to bludgeon his mother-in-law to death. He then turned on his father-in-law, attempting unsuccessfully to choke him to death. Covered with blood, Parks got back in his car and drove straight to a nearby police station and confessed, turning himself in, stating "I think I have just killed two people." At trial, Parks argued that he was sleepwalking and thus automatistic and not criminally liable. In his defence, a doctor testified as to his mental state at the time of the murder. From the doctor's evidence, it was determined that the accused was in fact sleepwalking at the time of the incident, and that he was suffering from a disorder of sleep rather than neurological, psychiatric, or other illness. Five neurological experts also confirmed that he was sleepwalking during the time of the incident. The jury acquitted Parks. The issue before the Supreme Court was whether the condition of sleepwalking can be classified as non-insane automatism or should be classified as "disease of the mind" (i.e. mental disorder automatism) and warrant a verdict of not guilty for reason of insanity. [...] The court upheld the acquittal, as the evidence presented a reasonable doubt about whether Parks acted voluntarily. Chief Justice Antonio Lamer held that the trial judge was correct in his analysis of the evidence and his decision not to characterize sleepwalking as a mental disorder.

gancho: Na síndrome da mão alienígena, uma das mãos age por conta própria. Uma paciente abotoava a blusa com uma mão enquanto a outra a desabotoava. Outra viu a mão tirar da boca o cigarro que a outra ia acender.
explicacao: A pessoa pega e manipula objetos sem querer, às vezes a ponto de ter de segurar a mão rebelde com a outra. O primeiro caso conhecido na literatura médica foi publicado em 1908 pelo neuropsiquiatra alemão Kurt Goldstein: uma mulher que, depois de um AVC, sentia o braço esquerdo como se fosse de outra pessoa e agindo independentemente da vontade dela. A síndrome é mais bem documentada em quem teve os hemisférios cerebrais separados por cirurgia contra epilepsia grave, mas também aparece depois de AVCs, tumores, infecções e doenças degenerativas. Quando o corpo caloso, que liga os hemisférios, está lesionado, as duas mãos podem agir uma contra a outra. Depois do episódio do cigarro, a paciente concluiu: "Acho que 'ele' não quer que eu fume". Em outro relato, uma mulher que tinha feito uma cirurgia no coração notou que a mão esquerda tinha "vida própria": desabotoava a roupa, tentava estrangulá-la enquanto dormia e brigava com a direita para atender o telefone. No filme Dr. Fantástico, de 1964, o personagem vivido por Peter Sellers parece ter a síndrome, porque não consegue conter a saudação nazista.

fontes.trecho: is a category of conditions in which a person experiences their limbs acting seemingly on their own, without conscious control over the actions. [...] The affected person may sometimes reach for objects and manipulate them without wanting to do so, even to the point of having to use the controllable hand to restrain the alien hand. [...] Alien hand syndrome is best documented in cases where a person has had the two hemispheres of their brain surgically separated, a procedure sometimes used to relieve the symptoms of extreme cases of epilepsy [...] It also occurs in some cases after brain surgery, stroke, infection, tumor, aneurysm, migraine and specific degenerative brain conditions [...] particularly in individuals who have sustained damage to the corpus callosum that connects the two cerebral hemispheres (see also Split-brain), the hands appear to be acting in opposition to each other. [...] one patient was observed putting a cigarette into her mouth with her intact, "controlled" hand (her right, dominant hand), following which her left hand rose, grasped the cigarette, pulled it out of her mouth, and tossed it away before it could be lit by the right hand. The patient then surmised that "I guess 'he' doesn't want me to smoke that cigarette." Another patient was observed to be buttoning up her blouse with her controlled dominant hand while the alien non-dominant hand, at the same time, was unbuttoning her blouse. [...] The first known case described in the medical literature appeared in a detailed case report published in German in 1908 by the preeminent German neuro-psychiatrist, Kurt Goldstein. In this paper, Goldstein described a right-handed woman who had had a stroke affecting her left side from which she had partially recovered by the time she was seen. However, her left arm seemed as though it belonged to another person and performed actions that appeared to occur independent of her will. [...] One week after undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting, she noticed that her left hand started to "live a life of its own". It would unbutton her gown, try to choke her while asleep and would automatically fight with the right hand to answer the phone. [...] In Stanley Kubrick's 1964 film Dr. Strangelove, the title character, played by Peter Sellers, apparently has  alien hand syndrome, as he cannot stop himself from doing the Nazi salute.

gancho: No século XVII, um filósofo perguntou: um cego de nascença que passasse a enxergar reconheceria pela visão um cubo que conhece pelo tato? Jovens operados entre 2007 e 2010 sugerem que não, ao menos de imediato.
explicacao: William Molyneux, cuja mulher era cega, mandou a pergunta numa carta a John Locke, que a reproduziu no "Ensaio sobre o entendimento humano", de 1689. Os dois achavam que não: o cego saberia como cubo e esfera se sentem ao toque, mas não como aparecem aos olhos. Leibniz discordava. Testar a resposta era quase impossível, porque os casos eram raríssimos: em 1971, um estudioso estimou que houve menos de vinte em mil anos. Em 2003, Pawan Sinha, professor do MIT, montou um programa, o Projeto Prakash, e encontrou cinco pessoas de 8 a 17 anos que, antes do tratamento, só distinguiam claro de escuro. Operadas entre 2007 e 2010, passaram a enxergar e foram testadas em até 48 horas. Elas distinguiam objetos pela visão quase tão bem quanto pelo tato, mas não conseguiam ligar uma coisa à outra: o acerto mal superava o chute. Os pesquisadores concluíram que a resposta a Molyneux é, em resumo, não. Três delas, testadas de novo depois de 5 dias, 7 dias e 5 meses, já acertavam de 80% a 90%. A ponte entre os sentidos, ao que parece, se aprende rápido, embora haja quem conteste a interpretação do estudo.

fontes.trecho: Molyneux's problem is a thought experiment in philosophy concerning immediate recovery from blindness. It was first formulated by William Molyneux, and notably referenced in John Locke's An Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1689). [...] The question was originally posed to Locke by philosopher William Molyneux, whose wife was blind. [...] the blind man, at first sight, would not be able with certainty to say which was the globe, which the cube, whilst he only saw them; though he could unerringly name them by his touch [...] Leibniz (German philosopher, 1646–1716) also discussed this problem, but derived a different answer. [...] One reason that Molyneux's Problem could be posed in the first place is the extreme dearth of human subjects who gain vision after extended congenital blindness. In 1971, Alberto Valvo estimated that fewer than twenty cases have been known in the last 1000 years. In 2003, Pawan Sinha, a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, set up a program in the framework of the Project Prakash and eventually had the opportunity to find five individuals who satisfied the requirements for an experiment aimed at answering Molyneux's question. Prior to treatment, the subjects (aged 8 to 17) were only able to discriminate between light and dark [...] The surgical treatments took place between 2007 and 2010, and quickly brought the relevant subject from total congenital blindness to fully seeing. A carefully designed test was submitted to each subject within the next 48 hours. [...] Although after restoration of sight, the subjects could distinguish between objects visually almost as effectively as they would do by touch alone, they were unable to form the connection between an object perceived using the two different senses. The correlation was barely better than if the subjects had guessed. They had no innate ability to transfer their tactile shape knowledge to the visual domain. However, the experimenters could test three of the five subjects on later dates (5 days, 7 days, and 5 months after, respectively) and found that the performance in the touch-to-vision case improved significantly, reaching 80–90%.

gancho: O experimento de Asch virou símbolo de conformismo: gente que repetia o erro do grupo ao comparar linhas. Mas dois terços das respostas desafiaram a maioria, e 95% dos voluntários resistiram ao menos uma vez.
explicacao: Em 1951, Solomon Asch reuniu grupos de oito universitários para dizer em voz alta qual de três linhas tinha o mesmo comprimento de uma linha de referência. Só um deles era voluntário de verdade, e respondia por último. Os outros eram atores que, em 12 rodadas, davam juntos a mesma resposta errada. Sem essa pressão, as pessoas erravam menos de 0,7% das vezes. Com ela, cerca de um terço das respostas acompanhou o erro do grupo, e 74% dos voluntários cederam pelo menos uma vez. O próprio Asch, porém, destacou que a independência predominou: 64,3% das respostas ficaram corretas. Mesmo assim, um levantamento de 2015 com 20 grandes livros didáticos achou só um que dizia que a maioria das respostas desafiou o grupo, e nenhum mencionava que 95% dos voluntários resistiram ao menos uma vez. Outros detalhes também costumam ficar de fora. Bastava um único ator dando a resposta certa para que a adesão ao erro da maioria despencasse. E todos os que cederam subestimaram quantas vezes tinham cedido.

fontes.trecho: In 1951, Asch conducted his first conformity laboratory experiments at Swarthmore College [...] Groups of eight male college students participated in a simple "perceptual" task. In reality, all but one of the participants were actors [...] Each participant was then asked to say aloud which line matched the length of that on the first card. [...] The group was seated such that the real participant always responded last. [...] In the control group, with no pressure to conform to actors, the error rate on the critical stimuli was less than 0.7%. In the actor condition also, the majority of participants' responses remained correct (64.3%) [...] An examination of all critical trials in the experimental group revealed that one-third of all responses were incorrect. [...] Overall, 74% of participants gave at least one incorrect answer out of the 12 critical trials. [...] All conforming respondents underestimated the frequency with which they conformed to the majority. [...] The presence of a single dissenter dramatically reduced conformity [...] Asch's 1956 report emphasized the predominance of independence over yielding [...] A 2015 survey found no change, with just 1 of 20 major texts reporting that most participant-responses defied majority opinion. No text mentioned that 95% of subjects defied the majority at least once.

gancho: No experimento de Milgram, 65% obedeceram até o choque máximo. Mas, quando dois falsos colegas se recusavam a continuar, só quatro de 40 iam até o fim. Com um amigo no papel da vítima, só três dos vinte pares.
explicacao: Os testes começaram em agosto de 1961, na Universidade Yale. O voluntário fazia o papel de "professor" e aplicava choques cada vez mais fortes num "aluno" a cada erro. Os choques eram falsos e o aluno era um ator, mas o voluntário não sabia. Antes, 40 psiquiatras tinham previsto que pouco mais de um décimo de um por cento iria até o fim. Na primeira versão, 65% chegaram aos 450 volts. O número ficou famoso, mas Milgram descreveu 19 variações, e elas mostram o quanto a obediência dependia da situação. Com as ordens dadas por telefone, ela caiu para 21%. Quando o voluntário tinha de segurar o braço do aluno sobre a placa de choque, 30% foram até o fim. Ao lado de dois colegas que se recusavam, só quatro de 40 continuaram; ao lado de um que obedecia, 37 de 40. Numa versão em que o voluntário levava um amigo para ser o aluno, só três dos vinte pares foram até o fim. Há críticas sérias: a psicóloga Gina Perry examinou os arquivos e concluiu que só metade dos participantes acreditou totalmente que era real, e que, desses, 66% desobedeceram. Ainda assim, uma meta-análise de repetições achou de 28% a 91% de obediência total, sem tendência de queda ao longo do tempo.

fontes.trecho: with every participant going up to 300 volts, and 65% going up to the full 450 volts. [...] The experiments began in August 1961 at Yale University [...] Unbeknownst to the subject, both slips said "teacher". [...] In reality, there were no shocks, and the learner simulated suffering increasing levels of pain from the shocks. [...] Milgram also polled forty psychiatrists from a medical school [...] they believed that "only a little over one-tenth of one percent of the subjects would administer the highest shock on the board." [...] Thomas Blass of the University of Maryland, Baltimore County performed a meta-analysis on the results of repeated performances of the experiment. He found that while the percentage of participants who are prepared to inflict fatal voltages ranged from 28% to 91%, there was no significant trend over time [...] She wrote that "only half of the people who undertook the experiment fully believed it was real and of those, 66% disobeyed the experimenter". [...] In Obedience to Authority: An Experimental View (1974), Milgram describes 19 variations of his experiment [...] In the variation where the learner's physical immediacy was closest—where the participant had to hold the learner's arm onto a shock plate—30 percent of participants completed the experiment. [...] For example, in Experiment 2, where participants received telephonic instructions from the experimenter, compliance decreased to 21 percent. [...] In Experiment 17, when two additional teachers refused to comply, only four of 40 participants continued in the experiment. [...] In that variation, 37 of 40 continued with the experiment. [...] In the RC, participants were required to bring a friend, with one becoming the teacher and the other the learner. Just three of the twenty pairs of friends in the study delivered each shock.

gancho: A história das 38 testemunhas inertes no assassinato de Kitty Genovese, que inspirou o estudo do efeito espectador, era exagerada. E um estudo com câmeras de rua viu alguém ajudar em mais de 90% das brigas.
explicacao: Kitty Genovese, de 28 anos, foi esfaqueada e morta em Nova York em março de 1964. Duas semanas depois, o New York Times afirmou que 38 testemunhas viram ou ouviram os ataques e que ninguém chamou a polícia até ela morrer. O caso levou os psicólogos John Darley e Bibb Latané a estudar o efeito espectador: em experimentos de laboratório, quem estava acompanhado tendia a ajudar bem menos do que quem estava sozinho. Mas a história original não se sustentou. Um artigo de 2007 não achou provas da presença de 38 testemunhas, nem de que elas tivessem visto o crime e ficado paradas. Em 2016, o próprio jornal chamou a reportagem de falha: ninguém viu o ataque inteiro, muitos acharam que ouviam uma briga de casal ou de bêbados, duas pessoas chamaram a polícia, e uma mulher de 70 anos saiu para amparar Kitty até a chegada do socorro. Em 2019, um estudo examinou mais de 200 gravações de câmeras de segurança de conflitos de rua no Reino Unido, na Holanda e na África do Sul. Em mais de 90% deles, uma ou mais pessoas intervieram, e mais espectadores aumentavam a chance de alguém agir. Uma meta-análise de 2011 já tinha visto que o efeito aparece nas emergências sem perigo, mas não nas perigosas.

fontes.trecho: The bystander effect was first demonstrated and popularized in the laboratory by social psychologists John M. Darley and Bibb Latané in 1968 after they became interested in the topic following the murder of Kitty Genovese in 1964. [...] These experiments have found that the presence of others inhibits helping, often by a large margin. [...] A 2011 meta-analysis found that the bystander effect was most likely to occur in non-dangerous emergencies but did not occur in dangerous emergencies. [...] Philpot et al. (2019) examined over 200 sets of real-life surveillance video recordings from the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and South Africa [...] They found that intervention was the norm, and in over 90% of conflicts one or more bystanders intervened to provide help. Increased bystander presence increased the likelihood that someone would intervene.

Kitty Genovese, a 28-year-old bartender, was raped and stabbed to death on March 13, 1964 [...] Two weeks after the murder, The New York Times published an article claiming that thirty-eight witnesses saw or heard the multiple attacks, and that none of them called the police until after she was dead. [...] In 2007, an article in American Psychologist found "no evidence for the presence of 38 witnesses, or that witnesses observed the murder, or that witnesses remained inactive". In 2016, the Times called its own reporting "flawed" [...] None saw the attack in its entirety. Only a few had glimpsed parts of it, or recognized the cries for help. Many thought they had heard lovers or drunks quarreling. There were two attacks, not three. And afterward, two people did call the police. A 70-year-old woman ventured out and cradled the dying victim in her arms until they arrived.

gancho: Antes de Robbers Cave, o famoso acampamento em que meninos viraram inimigos, houve um ensaio em 1953 dado como fracasso. Segundo um membro da equipe, colegas derrubaram uma barraca para atiçar a rivalidade.
explicacao: No estudo clássico de 1954, a equipe do psicólogo Muzafer Sherif levou 22 meninos de onze e doze anos, que não se conheciam, a um acampamento de verão em Oklahoma. Em dois grupos que disputavam prêmios em jogos, eles passaram a se hostilizar; depois, tarefas que exigiam cooperação reduziram a tensão. O estudo virou referência sobre como a competição por recursos gera conflito. Mas Robbers Cave foi a terceira e última tentativa de uma série iniciada em 1949. Na de 1953, que Sherif depois considerou um fracasso, um menino perguntou para que serviam os microfones pendurados no refeitório, e outro achou um caderno da equipe com anotações sobre as reações dos grupos, confirmando o boato de que aquilo era um experimento para fazê-los brigar. Um membro da equipe relembrou à psicóloga Gina Perry, que investigou os arquivos, o desânimo ao ver colegas derrubarem uma barraca na esperança de que um grupo culpasse o outro. Inflar o placar de uma equipe para aumentar a rivalidade foi comum em 1953 e em 1954. E, nos estudos anteriores, os meninos chegaram a se unir contra um inimigo comum e, às vezes, contra os próprios pesquisadores, sinal de que percebiam a manipulação.

fontes.trecho: The 1954 Robbers Cave experiment (or Robbers Cave study) by Muzafer Sherif and Carolyn Wood Sherif represents one of the most widely known demonstrations of RCT. The Sherifs' study was conducted over three weeks in a 200-acre summer camp in Robbers Cave State Park, Oklahoma, focusing on intergroup behavior. In this study, researchers posed as camp personnel, observing 22 eleven- and twelve-year-old boys who had never previously met [...] wherein the groups were entered into competition with one another in various camp games. [...] Valued prizes were awarded to the winners. This caused both groups to develop negative attitudes and behaviors towards the outgroup. [...] During this stage, tensions between the groups were reduced through teamwork-driven tasks that required intergroup cooperation. [...] In two earlier studies, the boys ganged up on a common enemy and, in fact, on occasion ganged up on the experimenters themselves, showing an awareness of being manipulated.

fontes.titulo: The view from the boys (Gina Perry, The Psychologist, British Psychological Society)
fontes.trecho: In all three of the intergroup conflict studies that Sherif conducted between 1949 and 1954, the boys showed their curiosity about the men running the camp and looked to the adults for guidance. [...] In the second study in 1953, which Sherif later wrote off as a failure, one boy asked the staff what the microphones hanging from the rafters in the mess hall were for. [...] A rumour amongst the boys that the camp was an experiment in which they were expected to fight one another was confirmed when one boy found a staff notebook including detailed observations of the groups' reactions. [...] For example, artificially inflating the scores of one team over another to increase rivalry was common in both the 1953 and 1954 studies. [...] One staff member recalled his dismay when other staff pulled one of the tents down in the hope that one group of boys would blame the other and the experiment would move to the next phase. [...] Robbers Cave was Sherif's third and final try in the intergroup conflict series

gancho: O Experimento da Prisão de Stanford, de 1971, virou prova de que qualquer um vira carrasco. Mas gravações mostram a equipe pedindo a um guarda que fosse mais duro, e o primeiro preso a surtar disse em 2017 que fingiu.
explicacao: Em agosto de 1971, Philip Zimbardo recrutou por anúncio de jornal universitários para uma "prisão" montada no porão do prédio de psicologia de Stanford. Os vinte e quatro escolhidos foram sorteados entre guardas e presos. O abuso psicológico dos guardas piorou dia a dia, e o estudo foi encerrado no sexto dia. Por décadas, foi contado como demonstração de que o papel e a situação transformam pessoas comuns. As críticas, porém, se acumularam. Gravações do site oficial do estudo, muito discutidas em 2017, mostram o assistente que fazia o papel de diretor da prisão incentivando um guarda a participar mais e ser mais "durão", pelo bem do experimento. Em 2018, o pesquisador francês Thibault Le Texier afirmou que os guardas foram orientados a agir de certos modos para confirmar conclusões escritas em boa parte antes do experimento. A maioria dos guardas disse depois que estava atuando de propósito. Douglas Korpi, o primeiro preso a sair, após um aparente colapso nervoso com 36 horas, disse em 2017 que fingiu para poder voltar a estudar para um exame. Zimbardo rejeitou as críticas, chamou as de Le Texier de ataque pessoal e afirmou que Korpi mentiu nessa entrevista.

fontes.trecho: Twenty-four participants were chosen after assessments of psychological stability and then assigned randomly to the role of prisoners or prison guards. [...] During the next five days, psychological abuse of the prisoners by the "guards" worsened. [...] He ended the experiment on the sixth day [...] Zimbardo claimed that Le Texier's article was mostly an ad hominem attack on him [...] study participants were recruited using an advertisement in the "help wanted" section of the Palo Alto Times and The Stanford Daily newspapers in August 1971 [...] The experiment was performed in a 35 ft (11 m) section of the basement of Jordan Hall, Stanford's psychology building. [...] Zimbardo assumed the role of Superintendent, and an undergraduate research assistant, David Jaffe, assumed the role of Warden. Digitized recordings available on the official SPE website were widely discussed in 2017, particularly one in which warden David Jaffe tried to influence the behavior of one of the guards by encouraging him to participate more and be more "tough" for the benefit of the experiment. [...] In 2018, Thibault Le Texier, a French researcher, questioned the scientific validity and merit of the experiment [...] he has established that the guards were asked directly to behave in certain ways in order to confirm Zimbardo's conclusions, which were largely written in advance of the experiment. [...] Most of the guards have stated since the SPE that they were intentionally acting. [...] The first prisoner to leave the experiment was Douglas Korpi, prisoner 8612. After 36 hours, he had an apparent mental breakdown [...] However, in a 2017 interview, Korpi stated that his breakdown had been fake, and that he did it only so that he could leave and return to studying for his Graduate Record Exam [...] Further, Zimbardo believes Korpi's 2017 interview was a lie.

gancho: Num clássico de 1969, baratas com uma plateia de outras baratas corriam mais rápido numa pista reta e mais devagar num labirinto. Em 2020, uma repetição com 120 baratas só confirmou a parte da lentidão.
explicacao: O estudo de Robert Zajonc e colegas testava uma ideia antiga da psicologia social. Em 1898, Norman Triplett notou que crianças enrolavam linha mais depressa quando competiam entre si. Zajonc propôs que a simples presença de outros funciona como uma fonte de excitação, que melhora o desempenho em tarefas simples e o piora nas complexas. Para ver isso em animais de cognição limitada, usou baratas, que fogem da luz: um holofote as fazia correr por uma pista reta ou por um labirinto, sozinhas ou com outras baratas olhando de caixas ao lado. O resultado virou presença constante em livros didáticos. Em 2020, pesquisadores alemães notaram que a interação famosa nunca tinha sido testada estatisticamente, e que o estudo provavelmente tinha poucos animais: só 40 nas condições decisivas. Eles reconstruíram o aparelho, seguiram o procedimento original o mais fielmente possível e usaram 120 baratas de uma espécie um pouco maior. Com plateia, as baratas ficaram mais lentas nas duas tarefas: a inibição se repetiu, mas não houve sinal de facilitação. Em humanos, uma meta-análise de 241 estudos achou efeitos pequenos nos dois sentidos.

fontes.titulo: Replicating Roaches: A Preregistered Direct Replication of Zajonc, Heingartner, and Herman's (1969) Social-Facilitation Study (Psychological Science)
fontes.trecho: Psychological Science 2020, Vol. 31(3) [...] Justus Liebig University Giessen [...] Fifty years ago, Zajonc, Heingartner, and Herman (1969) conducted a famous experiment on social enhancement and inhibition of performance in cockroaches. A moderating effect of task difficulty on the effect of the presence of an audience, as revealed by impaired performance in complex tasks and enhanced performance in simple tasks, was presented as the major conclusion of this research. However, the researchers did not test this interaction statistically. [...] Results revealed main effects for task difficulty, with faster running times in the runway than the maze, and for audience, with slower running times when the audience was present than when it was absent. There was no interaction between the presence of an audience and task difficulty. Although we replicated the social-inhibition effect, there was no evidence for a social-facilitation effect. [...] analysis of 241 studies (Bond & Titus, 1983) found a small facilitation effect in simple tasks [...] has been highly cited in textbooks [...] Moreover, the study is very likely to have been underpowered (with N = 40 for the critical [...] We precisely rebuilt the apparatus and followed the original procedure as closely as possible. [...] the cockroaches we used (Blaberus craniifer) are slightly larger than the ones in the original study (Blatta orientalis). [...] the starting box was illuminated with a floodlight to make the cockroach start running. [...] We decided to triple the sample size of the original study (resulting in a total sample of 120)

Zajonc's generalized drive hypothesis was the first theory that addressed why the presence of others increased performance sometimes yet decreased it at other times. He argued that the presence of others serves as a source of arousal, and heightened arousal increases the likelihood of an organism to do better on well-learned or habitual responses. For this reason, arousal improves performance on simple, or well-learned tasks, but impairs performance on complex, or not well-learned tasks. [...] In 1898, Norman Triplett pioneered research on social facilitation by studying the competitive nature of children. In this study, each child was given a string and was told to wind it. He found that children performed much better while they were competing with one another [...] In 1969, Zajonc, Heingartner, and Herman found evidence for social facilitation in animals with limited or no cognitive processing.

gancho: O "número de Dunbar", de 150 relações estáveis por pessoa, saiu de uma conta com cérebros de primatas. Refeita com dados atualizados, a conta deu margens de erro como de 4 a 520 pessoas: largas demais para valer.
explicacao: Nos anos 1990, o antropólogo britânico Robin Dunbar notou que, entre primatas, o volume do neocórtex parece limitar quantos membros do grupo cada animal consegue acompanhar. Em 1992, com dados de 38 gêneros de primatas, projetou para humanos um grupo médio de 148 pessoas, arredondado para 150. Ele mesmo tratou o resultado como exploratório, porque a margem de erro já era grande: de 100 a 230. Numa definição informal, seriam as pessoas com quem você não se sentiria constrangido de se juntar, sem convite, para um drinque, se as encontrasse num bar. O número ficou famoso e chegou a orientar empresas: uma agência de viagens australiana se reorganizou em "tribos" de no máximo 150 pessoas. Mas uma reanálise com dados atualizados e outros métodos filogenéticos chegou a médias de 69 a 109 ou de 16 a 42 pessoas, com intervalos de confiança de 4 a 520 e de 2 a 336. Os autores concluíram que não dá para derivar desse jeito um limite cognitivo para os grupos humanos. Dunbar respondeu que a conta deveria usar só dados de símios (gibões, orangotangos, chimpanzés, bonobos e gorilas), poucos demais para uma análise estatística, segundo os críticos. Já estudos de campo nos Estados Unidos estimaram uma média de 290 laços por pessoa.

fontes.trecho: This number was first proposed in the 1990s by Robin Dunbar, a British anthropologist who found a correlation between primate brain size and average social group size. [...] Dunbar explained the principle informally as "the number of people you would not feel embarrassed about joining uninvited for a drink if you happened to bump into them in a bar." [...] The number of social group members a primate can track appears to be limited by the volume of the neocortex. [...] In 1992, Dunbar used the correlation observed for non-human primates to predict a social group size for humans. Using a regression equation on data for 38 primate genera, Dunbar predicted a human "mean group size" of 148 (casually rounded to 150), a result he considered exploratory because of the large error measure (a 95% confidence interval of 100 to 230). [...] Flight Centre, an Australian travel agency, applied Dunbar's number when reorganising the firm into "families" (stores), "villages" (clusters of stores) and "tribes" (aggregates of villages up to a maximum of 150 people). [...] came up with an estimated mean number of ties, 290, which is roughly double Dunbar's estimate. [...] A replication of Dunbar's analysis on updated complementary datasets using different comparative phylogenetic methods yielded wildly different numbers. Bayesian and generalized least-squares phylogenetic methods generated approximations of average group sizes between 69–109 and 16–42, respectively.
